header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rem:anonymous:m016:norm, from the Referenzkorpus Mittelhochdeutsch, ReM 2.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.

notes.77v.19: 77v.21: the verse 'who made heaven and earth' breaks off after et; [earth] is supplied. 77v.23 nonne eo meatu per angelum maiestatis plus escare is garbled Latin, translated tentatively. 78r.2 talpone: perhaps the talpa, a creeping swelling or ulcer named after the mole. 78r.8 heiternezzelen is read as eiternezzel, stinging nettle. welliz (78r.6) may also mean 'boil it'.

nodes.text: and make a powder, and give it to your sheep. For horses that worms harm: tie around the neck
a bone of a dead horse; at once the worms die. For one whom a worm bites:
“Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and [earth].” Christ was sitting on a stone and held a rod
in his hand and said, “Lord, if these worms are alive, let them die; and if dead,
let them come out; may they feed no more in that passage, by the angel of majesty.”
Sing the Our Father three times, and say: “Lord, free this servant or handmaid N. from [the]
worm, from canker and *talpo*, and from all worms. Worm, I command you [by] God's
words and [those] of Saint Job and his holy children, that you bite this man or this
woman no more, neither by day nor by night.” Against the falling
sickness: take swallows from the nest, and cut off their heads, and mix white
frankincense with that blood until it becomes as thick as dough; roll it all together,
and when the moon first waxes or wanes, give it to drink. For
jaundice: boil the stinging nettle with the root and give it him to
drink for nine days: on the first day one spoonful, on the 2nd day 2, on the 3rd day 3, each day
one more; on the ninth day give him nine. Take the lizard
and lay it alive on the sick person's navel and bind [it]; all the sickness
that is in the patient goes into the lizard. If a sick person suddenly falls dumb,
boil pennyroyal in vinegar and hold it to his nostrils, and at once he speaks.
